shared_scope: All varieties, projectivity, smooth models and complex analytic structures retain their individual source hypotheses. A symmetric product X_m is the finite quotient X^m/S_m; d_1(Z), the big collision locus, reduced exceptional divisors and natural orbifold multiplicities are different source objects, and their definitions remain attached.

The rational quotient has a separate positive-genus curve-base branch: m<g uses B_m and m>=g uses its Jacobian image. The uniruledness exception is m>g, not m>=g. Source compact-Kahler remarks are retained as author extensions, not rewritten as new primary hypotheses.

The core-map theorem assumes n>=2 and base dimension p!=1, with p=0 trivial and smooth-model/bimeromorphic meaning. Its curve-base result has D_c=0 and threshold m=g; for nonzero orbifold base divisor the finite-cover corollary gives an eventual bound depending on(B,D_c). Remark4.8's sharper g(B)+deg(D_c) threshold is unproved context.

The dense-entire-curve proof is fully written for G=P1 and C of genus g>1 with m>=g; the elliptic G branch is described by the author as the same construction after substituting its universal cover. Retain that exact compressed branch without supplying a new proof or counting it separately. Question2 for arbitrary rationally connected G remains open, and the dense curve is not claimed to avoid the collision locus.

K3 dominability requires Pic(S)=Z generated by an ample L of degree2(g-1), g>1. The map from C^(2g) is transcendental meromorphic and covers a nonempty Zariski open U. The countable interpolation consequence is for P contained in U; arbitrary projective/nonprojective K3 surfaces and arbitrary Hilbert powers remain author expectations.

The jet criterion keeps k,r,d positive, A very ample, the precise Green-Griffiths base-locus condition, and the strict d/r>2m(m-1) inequality. Its target is the resolution's exceptional divisor union the preimage of d_1(Z). Introductory proper-Z and technical subset-Z versions remain distinct; the literal m=1-sensitive compensation formula is not repaired or given an added endpoint assumption.

The higher-subvariety result keeps property H_(Sigma,A), Sigma proper, A ample, its all-subvariety/existential q,r quantifiers, and codimension at most n-2 outside the singular and d_1(Sigma) loci. It does not prove the separate conjecture about the exceptional locus or all smaller-dimensional subvarieties.
